sentences.text: A boat has one job above all others: keep the water on the outside.
Today is about the hull that does it, and what to do when it doesn’t.
We start with shape, because shape decides how a boat behaves.
A displacement hull pushes through the water.
Her top speed, called hull speed, is limited by her waterline length, and no amount of horsepower will change it much.
A planing hull climbs up and skims on the surface once she has enough power and speed.
That’s how most charter boats travel.
A semi-displacement hull falls in between.
Now look at the bottom itself.
A deep-V cuts through chop and rides smoother.
A flat bottom is very stable at rest and floats in shallow water, but what does she do in a head sea?
Every hull is a trade, and you should know which trade you bought.
